text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuania was excluded from the first round of countries selected by the European Commission to begin EU entry talks. The government says it will strive to prove its readiness before EU governments make a final decision in Luxemburg in December.
- Deputy Health Minister Danute Kuchinskiene hit a rytas journalist in her office in response to a critical article.
- The council of parliament decided that MPs will not be allowed to take their weapons into parliament. Deputies are allowed to acquire guns for self-defense.

- The privatisation commission approved the terms of the privatisation of the Hotel Lithuania and decided that the initial price for the bid will be 44 million litas. The state owns 70 percent of the hotel.
- The chairman of Property Bank, which manages bad loans, said in an interview to the newspaper that the country's banking sector is not transparent enough.
- Mazeikiu Nafta oil refinery posted an 18.1 million litas net profit for the first half of the year compared to 56.4 million litas in losses in the same period in 1996.
- Birzhu Pipelines, crude and related products transporter, posted a 13.99 million litas net profit for the first six moths of the year and targets 40 million litas for 1997.
- Financial expert Margarita Starkevichiute called for more transparancy in the privatisation of the two state-run banks which the government has committed itself to selling.

- Transport minister Algis Zhvaliauskas said in an interview with the newspaper that the government intends to preserve the state's influence in the Lithuanian Sea Shipping company slated for privatisation earlier this year.
- Hotel room prices in Vilnius range from 20 litas to 1,200 litas. The city's 40 hotels are only half full though the tourist season has reached its peak.
